original_draft: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles. The right side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen, and the left side pumps oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body. The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it must push blood through the whole systemic circulation. A resting adult heart typically beats between 60 and 200 times per minute. Valves keep blood flowing in one direction; the mitral valve sits between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Each heartbeat starts in the sinoatrial node, a cluster of cells in the wall of the right atrium.
final_answer: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles. The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it must push blood through the whole systemic circulation. A resting adult heart typically beats between 60 and 100 times per minute. Valves keep blood flowing in one direction; the mitral valve sits between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Each heartbeat starts in the sinoatrial node, a cluster of cells in the wall of the right atrium.
